_comment: Copy this to config.json and edit. The token is generated automatically on first run if you leave it empty.

drobo._comment: 'drobo5n' talks to a real Drobo (the default); 'mock' runs the built-in simulator instead. host can be a static IP ('10.0.0.50'), 'auto' (or left blank) to find the device automatically -- no static IP/DHCP reservation needed -- or a mix: set 'hostname' to a known mDNS name like 'MyDrobo.local' as a second way to relocate it. expected_esa_id pins auto-discovery to one physical device (its permanent hardware serial -- printed in the agent log on first successful connect, so you can paste it in); leave it blank for first-run pairing. manual_discovery_ips are addresses you know, tried BEFORE the mDNS browse -- use these when your network filters multicast (many corporate LANs, guest SSIDs and some consumer routers do), which is when browsing returns nothing however long it listens; they say where to look, never what to trust, so identity checks still apply in full. discovery_sweep opts into a bounded subnet scan as a last resort if mDNS is blocked on your network; it's off by default because it's the slowest option.

updates._comment: DORMANT BY DEFAULT and that is the shipping state. The update machinery is built (agent/drobo_agent/updates.py) so it exists before it is needed rather than being assembled in a hurry on release day. With enabled false it opens no sockets and contacts nothing at all -- not a default endpoint that 404s, but no network activity whatsoever. To switch on later: set enabled true and point manifest_url at an https:// JSON file carrying version, download_url and sha256. The agent will only ever TELL you an update exists; downloading and installing stay a human decision, and an announcement without a valid SHA-256 is refused rather than shown.

notify._comment: Add 'ntfy' to backends and set a long random topic name to get alerts on your phone. Add 'email' to backends and fill the email block for SMTP alerts, which is what the original Drobo Dashboard did -- the agent sends them, not the Drobo, so an alert still arrives when the Drobo itself is the thing that is unreachable. The password lives here and nowhere else: this file is gitignored, and the password is never logged, never returned by the API, and never shown in the Windows app.

photos._comment: target_dir is where phone uploads land. Point it at a share on the Drobo.
